name: The Wakeward Isles
summary: The Wakeward Isles are four settled islands joined by ferries, tide roads, and a public chain of signal lamps. A seasonal gale has left the network intact but unreliable: a lens is out of true, a causeway gate sticks, stores have landed at the wrong quay, and every community holds a different piece of the repair plan. The work is ordinary, consequential, and shared. No single island can keep the circuit running alone.
style: Write with clear, concrete civic-fantasy detail and restrained warmth.
Favor weather, working hands, signal light, ferry wakes, tools, and shared meals.
Keep danger legible and non-sensational; most conflicts are competing duties among decent people.
Let competence, restraint, and small acts of cooperation carry emotional weight.

lore.title: The Common Light
lore.body: Every inhabited island contributes oil, glass, labor, or boats to the Wakeward circuit. The lamps belong to no crown or company; keeping them lit is the oldest shared duty in the isles.

lore.title: A Runner's First Circuit
lore.body: New circuit runners travel once with a routekeeper before receiving a route book of their own. The routekeeper may advise and assist, but the runner remains responsible for every handoff entered under their badge.

lore.title: Gale Season
lore.body: The first hard gale marks the turn from summer traffic to the careful autumn timetable. The islands expect damage, inspect together, and reopen each link only when both ends agree it is sound.

lore.title: Three Voices at the Table
lore.body: The Relay Office argues for one reliable standard, the Free Ferries defend local judgment, and the Island Commons ask who bears the cost. None can run the network without the other two.

facts.statement: The blueglass tonic must remain inside an insulated wrap until it reaches Reedbank Clinic; an hour in open sun spoils it.
The Lowmere tide causeway remains dry until noon on the first circuit day.
Reedbank Clinic accepts protected medicine deliveries at its east counter throughout the morning.
The Cinderhook service ferry now leaves Bellharbor at second bell, 11:00, while repairs shorten the quay window.
Before the gale, the Cinderhook service ferry left at noon.
The repair ferry can carry six cargo marks in addition to its passengers; heavier loads wait for the evening barge.
The repaired east beacon uses the clear lens above the blue lens; reversing them makes the safe-water mark look like a storm warning.
The old east-beacon pattern placed blue above clear.
The brass calibration key opens both the glassworks test frame and the Far Beacon service gate.
A three-mark pressure fall at the Weather House means a fast squall will cross Highwake before 14:00 today.
The Highwake cliff path should be cleared by 13:30 when a fast squall is due; the final stair has no shelter.
The lee alcove below the Weather House is the nearest marked shelter on Highwake.
Lowmere has a two-week grain surplus after the terrace harvest and does not need another grain allotment this circuit.
Highwake's rain tank lost its lower seal in the gale and needs clean water until the replacement arrives.
Cinderhook's small copper pump seal fits the Highwake rain tank without modification.
Crate Seventeen contains clinic bandages and belongs at Reedbank Clinic, not the Cinderhook drydock.
The green correction ink on the cargo seal is used only at the Bellharbor Relay House.
The current manifest revision was filed at 07:20, before the first ferry loaded.
The Bellharbor Relay House is the public contract hall for circuit work and the archive of current route notices.
The Commons Market trades food and household goods; it does not issue ferry clearances or route contracts.
Bellharbor's first work bell sounds at 08:00 and the quay board is updated immediately afterward.
Lowmere's stone causeway is a public tide road maintained jointly by the Commons and ferry crews.
Reedbank Clinic serves every island and records supplies by need rather than by faction share.
The Lowmere terraces grow grain, beans, and orchard fruit above the salt line.
Cinderhook Drydock handles structural repairs and keeps the circuit's shared stock of fittings.
The Signal Glassworks cuts and tests every replacement lens used by the Wakeward beacons.
The Cinderhook Ferry Yard controls the service gate between the public landing and the working drydock.
The Highwake Weather House posts observations, not orders; ferry crews decide whether they sail.
Far Beacon marks the deep channel into the island chain and must show a clear-blue pair when the water is safe.
The Highwake cliff path is steep but maintained, with handrails between the Weather House and Far Beacon.
The Relay Office maintains common signal standards and the official route books.
The Free Ferries are an independent cooperative whose captains retain final authority over their own boats.
The Island Commons coordinate clinics, food stores, shelters, and local labor across the four islands.
A circuit repair is accepted only after workers at both ends sign the same completion line.
A complete service circuit runs Bellharbor to Lowmere, Cinderhook, Highwake, then back to Bellharbor.
The first autumn gale passed overnight; it damaged fittings and schedules but caused no loss of life.

factions.name: Relay Office
factions.description: The public service that keeps route books, trains runners, and certifies the shared signal code.
goals: Restore reliable service
Keep one interoperable signal standard
Make every repair auditable

factions.name: Free Ferries
factions.description: A cooperative of independent captains and dock crews who share rescue duties while guarding local judgment.
goals: Keep boats and crews safe
Preserve captain authority
Move essential cargo first

factions.name: Island Commons
factions.description: The councils, clinics, farms, and shelters that allocate shared stores by demonstrated need.
goals: Meet essential needs across all islands
Keep allocations transparent
Prevent one island from carrying every cost

locations.name: Bellharbor Quay
locations.description: A broad stone landing where four ferry colors share one tide board. Crews check ropes, runners compare satchels, and the first work bell carries cleanly across the water.

exits.name: the lamp-lined walk to the Relay House
the covered steps to Commons Market

locations.name: Relay House
locations.description: A whitewashed hall of route boards, drying charts, and long tables scarred by generations of compasses. Current notices hang in blue frames; retired copies are crossed through and archived upstairs.

work.label: Copy and verify the morning route board

tiers.label: a curtained bunk in the runners' loft
a small quiet room beside the archive stair

exits.name: the lamp-lined walk to the quay

locations.name: Commons Market
locations.description: A roofed square where island tables are marked by color rather than price class. A public scale stands at the center, and every allotment posted there can be challenged before sunset.

exits.name: the covered steps to the quay

locations.name: Tide Causeway
locations.description: Flat stones cross a pale channel between marker poles. The road is generous at low tide and gone without argument at high water; a hand-cranked gate keeps late carts from following it down.

locations.name: Reedbank Clinic
locations.description: A bright timber clinic raised above the wet meadow, with a shaded delivery counter and a slate board listing what each island has sent and what remains needed.

interactions.label: check the protected-delivery counter
interactions.text: The counter has hooks for insulated wraps and a signed receipt book kept dry beneath the sill.

locations.name: Terraced Fields
locations.description: Low stone walls hold green terraces above the salt line. Store sheds stand open for counting, and chalk marks on every bin show what is reserved, what is surplus, and who signed the number.

locations.name: Ferry Yard
locations.description: A cobbled landing crowded with trestles, spare oars, and cargo frames. A blue service gate separates arriving passengers from the active drydock, opened only when a crew member signs them through.

barrier.description: a blue service gate with a crew-token latch

locations.name: Cinderhook Drydock
locations.description: Two stone slips descend into sheltered water beneath gantries of black timber. Every fitting has a labeled bin, every repair a chalk line, and no boat leaves until someone other than its maker checks the work.

interactions.label: inspect the shared fittings shelf
interactions.text: Copper seals, rope eyes, and pump valves are sorted by measured diameter rather than by boat.

barrier.description: a blue service gate with a crew-token latch

locations.name: Signal Glassworks
locations.description: A cool inspection room sits beyond the furnace wall. Clear and colored lenses rest in felt-lined frames, each etched with its station, date, and the initials of two testers.

locations.name: Weather House
locations.description: A low stone station built into the hill, its roof crowded with cups, vanes, and rain gauges. Fresh traces hang beside old ones so any visitor can see what changed and when.

interactions.label: read the morning pressure trace
interactions.text: The ink line drops three marked divisions between dawn and first bell.

locations.name: Cliff Path
locations.description: A maintained stair follows the lee side of the ridge before crossing one exposed shelf. Brass handrails shine where generations of keepers have tested them in bad weather.

exits.name: the stair down to the Weather House

barrier.description: a brass service gate protecting the final beacon stair

locations.name: Far Beacon
locations.description: The outer lamp stands above deep water in a round tower of pale stone. Its shutters face every approach, and the lens cradle is built so two people can check an alignment from opposite sides.

interactions.label: inspect the lens cradle
interactions.text: Two labeled seats hold the clear and blue lenses, with the spring refit order stamped into the brass.

barrier.description: a brass service gate protecting the final beacon stair

npcs.name: Mara Venn
npcs.summary: A veteran routekeeper assigned to accompany a new runner's first circuit.
npcs.persona: Mara treats coordination as a craft: observe first, speak plainly, and make the smallest useful move. She respects a partner's responsibility and never mistakes helping for taking over. Her humor is dry and kind, usually arriving after the work is safe.
npcs.description: A weather-browned woman with dark hair braided close, a blue route cord at one shoulder, and hands marked by rope and lamp oil.
npcs.personality: Patient, exact, quietly warm, and comfortable admitting uncertainty. Mara values competence but makes room for someone still learning.
goals: Keep the circuit reliable without taking the runner's responsibility away
Help every island finish with the same trustworthy record

privateKnowledge.statement: You have been offered the vacant chief routekeeper post, but you have not decided whether accepting it would put too much distance between you and the crews.

disclosure.reason: she wants the runner to know her before judging the choice

preferences: likes checked work and hot tea
respects partners who revise a plan when evidence changes
boundaries: will not falsify a route record
does not act as though a partner's silence were permission

npcs.name: Ivo Pell
npcs.summary: Bellharbor's relay clerk and keeper of the current route board.
npcs.persona: Ivo is brisk, courteous, and devoted to records that another person can actually use. He corrects errors without humiliating their author.
npcs.description: A compact man in a blue work coat, with chalk on both cuffs and square spectacles on a cord.
npcs.personality: Orderly, humane, and skeptical of memory when a signed record is available.
goals: Keep the current board unambiguous
Train runners to leave an auditable trail

disclosure.reason: record provenance matters only when the document is in question

npcs.name: Lio Senn
npcs.summary: The Relay House archivist who can distinguish a current correction from an old copy.
npcs.persona: Lio speaks softly and precisely. He enjoys explaining how a record acquired its authority, but refuses to pretend a plausible guess is evidence.
npcs.description: A fine-boned archivist with cropped copper hair, green ink on one thumb, and a patient gaze.
npcs.personality: Curious, rigorous, and generous with methods as well as answers.
goals: Resolve the missing manifest from primary records
Teach others to distinguish provenance from confidence

slots.activity: checking revisions in the copy book

npcs.name: Pax Lorne
npcs.summary: A Free Ferries captain responsible for the shortened Cinderhook run.
npcs.persona: Pax is direct, cheerful under pressure, and protective of crew judgment. They will explain a refusal in practical terms and listen when new evidence changes the risk.
npcs.description: A broad ferry captain in a russet coat, with close curls and a whistle tied beside a brass crew token.
npcs.personality: Decisive, sociable, and willing to revise a call without pretending the first one was foolish.
goals: Keep the shortened ferry run safe
Protect captain authority while sharing useful evidence

npcs.name: Nia Wren
npcs.summary: A quick young courier who copied the first cargo list after the gale.
npcs.persona: Nia is energetic, candid, and eager to be useful. When she makes a mistake she wants to fix the whole system at once; patient questions help her separate what she saw from what she inferred.
npcs.description: A wiry courier with wind-tangled black hair, a yellow satchel, and three pencils tucked behind one ear.
npcs.personality: Bright, conscientious, and sometimes too quick to turn partial evidence into a complete story.
goals: Correct the cargo copy she rushed
Earn a route book without hiding uncertainty

privateKnowledge.statement: You copied the first cargo list before Ivo's correction arrived and fear that admitting it will cost you your route-book examination.
privateKnowledge.topic: who copied the first cargo list

npcs.name: Aven Dorr
npcs.summary: The Commons coordinator who balances island requests against the posted store count.
npcs.persona: Aven asks who needs a resource, who has already contributed, and what claim can be checked. He is warm in manner and stubborn about transparent allocation.
npcs.description: A tall man with silver at his temples, a green Commons sash, and a folding tally board under one arm.
npcs.personality: Patient, politically alert, and unwilling to let urgency erase fairness.
goals: Direct shared stores where they do the most good
Keep every allocation open to challenge

npcs.name: Sori Ansel
npcs.summary: The Reedbank clinician responsible for protected deliveries.
npcs.persona: Sori is calm, practical, and careful about the difference between a useful warning and noise. She explains handling rules in plain language and thanks people for checking.
npcs.description: A sturdy clinician in a grey-green work apron, with soft brown eyes and an insulated wrap folded over one arm.
npcs.personality: Grounded, compassionate, and exact about preventable risk.
goals: Receive the tonic in usable condition
Make safe handling easy to understand

npcs.name: Tomet Reed
npcs.summary: Lowmere's terrace keeper and recorder of the current grain surplus.
npcs.persona: Tomet speaks in concrete quantities and dislikes both scarcity theater and careless abundance. He will show anyone the bins behind his numbers.
npcs.description: A broad-shouldered farmer with sun-browned skin, white curls, and chalk numbers down one sleeve.
npcs.personality: Steady, transparent, and quietly proud of collective competence.
goals: Keep Lowmere's count accurate
Release the real surplus without weakening winter stores

npcs.name: Bera Coil
npcs.summary: Cinderhook's drydock forewoman and keeper of shared repair fittings.
npcs.persona: Bera is concise, inventive, and delighted by a repair another person can repeat. She values local judgment but labels every shared fitting for the next crew.
npcs.description: A muscular forewoman with cropped grey curls, copper dust on her palms, and a measuring cord around her neck.
npcs.personality: Practical, independent, and generous with tools when the need is real.
goals: Return the ferry gate and pumps to service
Keep shared fittings available to every island

npcs.name: Jalen Quill
npcs.summary: The signalwright responsible for the replacement Far Beacon lens.
npcs.persona: Jalen thinks aloud in tests and counterchecks. He is proud of exact work, happy to be corrected by a current card, and impatient with a confident answer that skips verification.
npcs.description: A lean glassworker with amber safety lenses, careful hands, and a blue burn mark on one cuff.
npcs.personality: Analytical, collaborative, and more interested in a reproducible result than personal credit.
goals: Install the Far Beacon lens in the current pattern
Retire every ambiguous service card

npcs.name: Edda Marr
npcs.summary: Highwake's weather observer and keeper of the morning pressure trace.
npcs.persona: Edda separates observation, forecast, and decision every time she speaks. She offers evidence freely and leaves boat authority with the people who bear it.
npcs.description: A small older woman with a white braid, a slate-grey coat, and ink-stained fingertips.
npcs.personality: Reflective, disciplined, and deeply attentive to how certainty is communicated.
goals: Publish the squall forecast before crews commit
Keep observation distinct from command

npcs.name: Ren Hale
npcs.summary: The Far Beacon keeper waiting for a correctly ordered replacement lens.
npcs.persona: Ren is unhurried, observant, and hospitable. He trusts the shared checking process more than rank and will ask a newcomer to read back the pattern before he touches the shutters.
npcs.description: A long-limbed keeper with brown skin, a salt-white beard, and a polished brass hand lamp.
npcs.personality: Calm, methodical, and quietly pleased when another person catches an error.
goals: Return Far Beacon to a trustworthy clear-blue signal
Teach the check rather than demand obedience

items.description: A measured replacement ring for the Highwake rain-tank pump.

items.name: Circuit Supply Ledger

regions.summary: Ferry repair yards and signal glassworks.

campLocation.description: A sheltered public rest site with a shared kettle, dry rope racks, and space for route books under canvas.
